nodes.label: Agent LED health mapping (ok / amber / red / idle)
nodes.rationale: Staleness is folded into health (via S47 healthOf) so one LED encodes both liveness and outcome. Blink is reserved for red/failed only — motion is an alarm channel, not decoration (§7), and it must respect the global reduced-motion rule. Missing status.json renders idle with no glow rather than an error, so an un-deployed agent is not indistinguishable from a broken one.
nodes.norm_label: agent led health mapping (ok / amber / red / idle)

nodes.label: agentManifest static roster
nodes.rationale: Roster identity (name, purpose, infra gha|pc|vps, cadence) is static and known at build time, while status is live from vault fixtures. Splitting the two means an agent that has never run still appears in the table as idle instead of silently missing.

nodes.label: Token-capped vault context pack
nodes.rationale: The agent reads the WHOLE vault but compresses each file into a compact digest under a hard token cap before the Claude compose call — the builder stays a pure function so the cap and the digest shape are testable without any live model call. Malformed model output retries once then fails loudly via runLog ok:false rather than writing a half-brief.

nodes.norm_label: s51 — telegram bot logs runs → appears on health

nodes.label: Always-on bot heartbeat cadence
nodes.rationale: Cadence semantics differ from cron agents: a long-poll bot is always on, so 'last run' would look permanently stale. A 15-minute heartbeat (ok:true, note 'polling') keeps the fleet board honest. Logging failures are swallowed with console.warn — telemetry must NEVER break message handling.

nodes.norm_label: s52 — supervisor report + proposal contracts + parsers

nodes.label: Proposal file contract (pending | approved | rejected)
nodes.rationale: A markdown file with frontmatter (agent, date, status) plus Change / Diff / Why sections is the whole control-plane state machine — no database, no API. An invalid status is treated as pending, the safe default, so a corrupt file can never be read as owner approval.

nodes.label: setProposalStatus — byte-surgical status flip
nodes.rationale: A pure text transform that flips ONLY the status line and byte-preserves everything else, proven by a byte-diff test. Round-tripping through a parser and re-serialiser would silently reformat the owner's own prose; the file is the source of truth, so the transform must be surgical rather than regenerative.

nodes.label: Two-step confirm-destructive approval
nodes.rationale: Approving a proposal lets an agent self-modify, so the tap is armed rather than immediate: first tap shows 'Confirm approve?', a second tap within 5s commits, otherwise it resets. Inherits v1 S17 / ADR-0013's confirm-destructive spirit. The write goes through the same transport seam as habitsWrite — no direct fs/git in components.

nodes.label: Proposals-only invariant (agent never self-modifies)

Enforced in code rather than by convention: status is a hardcoded literal so no code path can emit 'approved', asserted by grep/test. The human gate lives in the PWA (S54), which makes owner approval the only route from proposal to change.

nodes.label: S56 — Git-history guard: shallow depth + log rotation
nodes.norm_label: s56 — git-history guard: shallow depth + log rotation

nodes.label: Shallow single-branch clone guarantee
nodes.rationale: Agents commit constantly (runs.jsonl, status.json, calendar rewrites), so vault history grows without bound and the PWA's in-browser clone slows. depth:1 + singleBranch is asserted via spies on BOTH transports (browser and bot) rather than assumed — and if already present, assert and move on, do not churn.

nodes.label: rotateJsonl / pruneNetworth log rotation
nodes.rationale: Append-only agent logs are split by month, N months kept in place and the rest archived to agents/<name>/archive/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl, with zero lines lost across files (sum-tested) and idempotence on a second run. Archiving rather than deleting keeps the audit trail the supervisor depends on.

nodes.label: S57 — Per-agent scoped tokens + shared push wrapper
nodes.norm_label: s57 — per-agent scoped tokens + shared push wrapper

nodes.label: Per-agent scoped PAT inventory
nodes.rationale: Every agent gets its OWN fine-grained PAT so revoking one leaves the rest untouched — the blast-radius pattern set by v1's BOT_VAULT_PAT. Scope is contents-write on LiveOS-VaultRepo only, and the token table records where each secret is stored (GH Actions secret / PC credential manager / VPS .env) plus rotation steps.

nodes.label: commitAndPush — pull-rebase-push retry wrapper
nodes.rationale: All agent pushes funnel through one wrapper that survives concurrent writers: stage ONLY the listed files, commit, pull --rebase, push, retry up to 3 with jittered backoff, then throw loud so the caller's runLog records ok:false. Path-partitioning makes rebases trivial, but rejects still happen on timing. Staging only listed files prevents an unrelated dirty file from riding along.

nodes.label: S58 — Tasks tab: slim Home, fold Up next/Later + Domains + Pulse
nodes.norm_label: s58 — tasks tab: slim home, fold up next/later + domains + pulse

nodes.label: Five-tab IA (Home · Tasks · Money · Career · Agents)
nodes.rationale: Home becomes ONLY the check-in surface; everything list-shaped moves out. Domains and Pulse stop being top-level tabs and become Segmented sub-nav segments inside Tasks — a re-parenting, not a rewrite, so DomainsMap and PulseView render verbatim. DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md is a LOCKED contract but owner feedback overrides it, so §5's 'six tabs, no more' must be edited in the same PR or the design-conformance eval correctly fails. Sole-App.tsx-toucher ownership transfers from S24 to S58.
nodes.norm_label: five-tab ia (home · tasks · money · career · agents)

nodes.label: S59 — Tab bar fits every screen
nodes.rationale: Fluid clamp() metrics over a scroller: same words at every width down to 320px, never icons or abbreviations. A horizontal-scroll fallback is allowed only if labels genuinely cannot fit, and then the track must show a partial next tab so the affordance reads. Asserted on computed layout (scrollWidth <= clientWidth), never a screenshot.
nodes.norm_label: s59 — tab bar fits every screen

nodes.label: S60 — Warmth becomes the background tint; Completion takes its vital tile
nodes.norm_label: s60 — warmth becomes the background tint; completion takes its vital tile

nodes.label: warmthTint — domain-weighted background blend
nodes.rationale: A pure module (no Date.now, no DOM) blends the 7 --d-* domain tokens weighted by WARMTH_OPACITY so the whole app is coloured by how hot the owner's domains are. Alpha is capped ≈0.10 because the tint sits UNDER frosted glass panels and text contrast is non-negotiable. Rendered as one static fixed inset-0 layer — no new requestAnimationFrame, so the reduced-motion contract needs no branch at all. Lives in Aurora, not App.tsx, because App.tsx is S58's hotspot that wave.

nodes.label: completionVital selector
nodes.rationale: Pure (tasks) → {value, sub} selector rendered through the shipped glass Vital so count-up and reduced-motion stay live. An empty vault renders the honest '—' placeholder, never 0% or 100% — §8's no-fake-real-data rule: 0/0 is not 100%.

nodes.label: S61 — GitTransport: recursive, non-.md vault reads (#158)
nodes.norm_label: s61 — gittransport: recursive, non-.md vault reads (#158)

nodes.label: Recursive vault enumeration with extension allowlist
nodes.rationale: _readFiles() walked a hardcoded flat list of top-level folders and kept only .md, so five consumer folders were silently invisible and were patched one string at a time (Habits #148, Calendar #151, Mail #154). agents/<name>/status.json is a directory deeper AND .json, which the one-string fix cannot reach. Fix the CLASS: recursive descent with a bounded depth plus an extension allowlist, so the hardcoded folder list stops being the thing that decides what the app can see — and Briefs/ is fixed for free.
nodes.norm_label: recursive vault enumeration with extension allowlist

nodes.label: VaultSync.list() pollution hazard
nodes.rationale: Twice-burned v2 lesson: every newly-surfaced file flows into list() and is run through parseTaskLine's /^- \[([ xX])\]…/ checkbox regex. Mail lines matched and needed an explicit continue; Calendar lines never did. For EVERY newly-surfaced path, diff its line format against that regex and either add a guard with a red-before-fix test or state in the PR why none is needed. .json bodies are a fresh risk. Companion rule: never construct the real lightning-fs backend in a test — the fingerprint is 'ReferenceError: navigator is not defined … DefaultBackend.init', all tests pass but vitest exits 1.

nodes.label: S62 — Config-check before the dynamic import (#155)
nodes.norm_label: s62 — config-check before the dynamic import (#155)

nodes.label: Synchronous config check before the dynamic import
nodes.rationale: Cards carried component-local short-circuits reading VITE_VAULT_REPO_URL to avoid paying the isomorphic-git / lightning-fs dynamic import before loadGit() threw — it pushed cockpitShell.test over its render budget. That works but bakes GitTransport's private config contract into components whose only dependency should be the VaultTransport interface. Fix it at the seam: do the synchronous if (!url) check inside GitTransport BEFORE the import, then every self-loading card gets the fast empty path for free and the component-local guards delete. Root-cause across siblings (TodayCard/HabitsCard never got the guard), not just the one the issue names.
nodes.norm_label: synchronous config check before the dynamic import

nodes.label: S63 — Remove the shell's AnimatePresence exit protocol (#173)
nodes.norm_label: s63 — remove the shell's animatepresence exit protocol (#173)

nodes.label: framer-motion presence acknowledgement protocol
nodes.rationale: AnimatePresence tracks exit completion through an acknowledgement protocol that a descendant joins IMPLICITLY — by declaring exit (ExitAnimationFeature.mount → register) or layout/layoutId (MeasureLayout's usePresence owes safeToRemove). No opt-in, no type-level signal. The obligation is edge-triggered and one-shot (update() bails on isPresent === prevIsPresent) and there is no timeout, watchdog or fallback. Under mode='wait' nextChildren = exitingChildren, so ONE missing ack = total blackout with invisible-but-clickable content still mounted; under mode='sync' the worst case is a ghost layer. The shell is a microkernel and tab panels are plugins; mode='wait' lets a plugin hang the core. Deleting the orphaned exit props is a symptom fix — the fuse, not the powder.

nodes.label: ADR-0015 — Shell owns no presence protocol
nodes.rationale: Records the two implicit registration classes (exit; layout/layoutId via MeasureLayout), the no-timeout finding, and the per-mode blast radius (wait = blackout, sync = ghost layer). Warranted as an ADR rather than a code comment because it constrains every future panel — strategic, not tactical. The rule is about the SHELL (no AnimatePresence in App.tsx), not 'no AnimatePresence anywhere'.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0015 — shell owns no presence protocol

nodes.label: S64 — Optimistic task writes, vault re-read off the write path (#174)
nodes.norm_label: s64 — optimistic task writes, vault re-read off the write path (#174)

nodes.label: Optimistic apply with targeted single-id rollback
nodes.rationale: The root cause was not only the missing optimistic setState but that a redundant FULL vault re-read (await refresh()) was serialized into user-visible latency — ~1.1s local commit plus ~8s network pull and reparse. VaultSync IS the cache: every mutation updates snapshot and lastFiles in place and RETURNS the persisted Task, a value useTasks discarded on all four paths. So: drop refresh() everywhere, apply the provider's return value, and pre-apply optimistically only where the hook can mirror provider semantics byte-for-byte (toggleDone, deleteTask) — never updateTask, whose empty-string-unsets and undefined-clears rules would drift if duplicated across the seam. Rollback is a targeted inverse patch on ONE id, never a whole-list restore. The rethrow is preserved because S72 depends on that signal.
nodes.norm_label: optimistic apply with targeted single-id rollback

nodes.label: Deferred-inversion latch (owedRef, XOR semantics)
nodes.rationale: Invariant: at most one un-settled provider op per id. A second tap during the settle window must not double-write, must not throw (MissionCard awaits onToggle uncaught, so it must return not throw), and must still flip synchronously — otherwise Undo is a dead click. One BIT per id, never a list: a further deferred call CLEARS the bit rather than adding a second, because the bit means 'the row is inverted relative to what the in-flight op will leave on the server' and two deferred flips cancel. The rejected sticky alternative passes tests (e)/(e2)/(e3) yet issues a follow-up for an even number of flips, so three rapid taps settle to done === false with a visible bounce — test (e4) exists solely to make that observable. It is a latch, not a queue; VaultSync.enqueue already serializes FIFO and a second queue would break the one-op-per-id invariant.

nodes.label: refresh() two-condition staleness guard
nodes.rationale: VaultSync.list() is NOT enqueued — only mutations go through the FIFO — so a list() and a write can be in flight simultaneously and settle in either order, and optimistic state widens the window because the user can click at t≈0. Sample localVersionRef before await provider.list(); discard the result if the version moved OR inFlightRef is non-empty. BOTH conditions are required: a write applied before list() sampled the counter leaves the counter unchanged, so the version check alone still lets a pre-write server list commit.

nodes.label: Anti-vacuity test harness rule (#120 lesson)
nodes.rationale: Drive pre-settle assertions with SYNCHRONOUS act(() => { void fn().catch(() => {}) }), never await act(async …): the async form drains microtasks and lets a master-shaped implementation reach its setState, making the test pass for the wrong reason. Every deferred exposes isSettled() and every pre-settle block LEADS with expect(isSettled()).toBe(false), mechanically proving the assertion is pre-settle. Every rollback/filter test needs a CONTROL (a sibling task, a good file alongside the ghost) because 'nothing ever changed' otherwise satisfies the final assertion. Never combine vi.useFakeTimers() with framer-motion's rAF driver. Test the invariant, not the incident: journey-replay of #173 in jsdom passed against broken master on all five cases.

nodes.label: S66 — Single owner for the vault FS (#176)
nodes.norm_label: s66 — single owner for the vault fs (#176)

nodes.label: getVaultTransport — module-level lazy single owner of FS_NAME
nodes.rationale: EIGHT independent GitTransport instances each constructed a LightningFS over the one 'lifeos-vault' IndexedDB store and lock — 7 read paths plus a fresh instance per habit tap on the write path. GitTransport.inflight was the right guard at the wrong scope: per-instance while the resource is per-process. S66 finishes the idea already in the file. LAZY memo, not eager const: eager construction is a module-import side effect, would revive #155's render budget and getVaultPat()'s blocking window.prompt. React context rejected on three grounds — it forces a Provider into the App.tsx hotspot, selfLoadTasks.ts is a module and cannot consume context (so you would need the singleton anyway — two mechanisms for one resource), and it models a process-global as tree-scoped state. Editing VaultSync.ts:88 alone covers both module singletons, keeping S66 out of the App.tsx lane.
nodes.norm_label: getvaulttransport — module-level lazy single owner of fs_name

nodes.label: In-place fs.init reset (non-stealing)
nodes.rationale: new LightningFS(FS_NAME, {wipe:true}) wipes the store BEFORE the mutex is ever acquired — the wiping instance never holds the lock — then Mutex2.release({force:true}) takes navigator.locks steal, breaking every held lock and rejecting the victims with an uncatchable AbortError (the rejecting promise is discarded inside the dependency and never enters our awaited chain, so no try/catch in _readFiles can reach it). Resetting through the EXISTING handle with fs.init(name,{wipe:true}) drains in-flight ops and releases the mutex through the normal path, so the subsequent steal has no local holder to victimise and grants immediately. Only one PromisifiedFS object exists, so multi-instance superblock divergence — the actual corrupter — is gone by construction. Hard constraint: the ADR-0010 commitsAhead === 0 gate stays byte-identical; (c) changes HOW we reset, never WHETHER it is safe to.

nodes.label: Ghost-file content-type guard
nodes.rationale: IdbBackend.readFile resolves undefined for a missing key instead of rejecting, and DefaultBackend's ENOENT throw is skipped because stat is truthy from the cached tree — so a corrupt store returns undefined WITHOUT throwing and the `as string` cast launders it past the type system. Downstream: VaultSync.list() TypeErrors on content.split, while the five self-loading cards produce NO error at all — TodayCard confidently renders 'no events today'. The silent variant is worse: the user's mental model is corrupted, not just their console. This guard is the only part of S66 that helps a user whose IndexedDB is ALREADY poisoned; single ownership prevents new corruption but heals nothing.

nodes.label: Shared readFiles aliasing hazard (defensive copy)
nodes.source_location: The aliasing hazard this fix INTRODUCES
nodes.rationale: The highest-probability way for S66 to introduce a new bug while fixing an old one. inflight collapses concurrent callers onto ONE promise, so every sharer gets the identical array of identical objects — and VaultSync mutates those entries in place (lastFiles = files, then fileEntry.content = newContent, plus lastFiles.push). Safe today only because each consumer has its own transport. After the singleton, five cards and both VaultSync instances alias one array with two mutators on it. Mandatory mitigation: readFiles() hands each caller a defensive copy, above inflight.

nodes.label: S68 — Surface capture write-failures instead of diverging silently (#178)
nodes.norm_label: s68 — surface capture write-failures instead of diverging silently (#178)

nodes.label: refresh() never-rejects contract
nodes.rationale: Tightening the CALLEE's contract repairs the uncaught rejection at App.tsx:67-71 WITHOUT editing App.tsx — which is how S68 stays out of the forbidden hotspot lane. The catch logs and returns; it does not rethrow, does not touch tasks, does not touch error. Documented as a contract in the JSDoc ('Never rejects. On failure the last-known list is retained and the reason is logged.'). A console.error spy in the test kills an empty catch {}.

nodes.label: CaptureSheet write-failure surface
nodes.rationale: The failure message is rendered by the component that OWNS the interaction, so no shell edit and no toast framework is needed. The raw error message is shown in dim beside the headline because it is what made #178 diagnosable from the deployed build. The retry affordance is the existing Add button — finally re-enables it and it already reads 'Add Task'. The single worst way to ship this: catching inside useTasks.addTask, which makes addTask resolve on failure, HomeView reaches setAddOpen(false), CaptureSheet unmounts and the user's typed text is destroyed with no message — strictly worse than #178. Second-worst: a catch that also calls setText('').

nodes.label: S72 — Open the undo window at click time (#182)
nodes.norm_label: s72 — open the undo window at click time (#182)

nodes.label: Toast pending gate + latest-ref dismiss timer
nodes.rationale: Two independent causes, and fixing either alone makes it worse: the toast was gated on a full write round-trip, and the dismiss timer started on MOUNT, so moving the toast earlier without a gate makes a 3s timer fire before an 8s write resolves. Fix: show at click time, start the countdown at SETTLE via a pending prop, with a latest-ref so the effect depends only on [pending] and never reschedules when onDismiss changes identity. The prop is `pending` (default false) not `settled` (which must default true and reads backwards) — pending keeps both call sites and all five existing tests compiling. pendingIds is NOT used: the undo re-issue is itself a toggleDone(id), so a per-id gate re-arms itself after the user already dismissed; the real question is per-toast, and both owners already hold the exact promise. The `p.id === id` guard is load-bearing, not defensive: complete A then B inside the window and A's late settle must not start B's countdown.
nodes.norm_label: toast pending gate + latest-ref dismiss timer

nodes.label: DISMISS_MS = 8000 counted from settle
nodes.rationale: 3s is the INFORMATIONAL toast number, not the ACTIONABLE one. Material's snackbar-with-action band is 4-10s and Gmail/Drive undo bars sit 5-10s; the action here is not cheap (notice a peripheral bottom-center pill, read a 160px-truncated title, move a thumb, hit the target) and undo is the only recovery once the row has left every ranked section. Not indefinite (becomes permanent chrome, multiplies the two-toast case), not 10s+ (overlaps the next completion in a multi-complete flow). Tactical by the strategic-vs-tactical test: one line, one stakeholder, reversible — so exported with exactly ONE literal assertion as a deliberate-change tripwire. Retraction on failure is not cosmetic: a surviving toast would read '"X" completed' next to X sitting undone, and its Undo would then COMPLETE the task.

nodes.label: PWA Emulation Testing Protocol
nodes.rationale: Slice B's PWA acceptance (installable + offline on Windows + Android) must be provable without owning two physical devices. Emulation replaces most of the manual HITL checklist; only the literal OS install gesture stays human-ish, and even that is emulated at Tier 3. Layered so the cheapest tier runs first and you stop as soon as confidence is sufficient.

nodes.label: Tier 0 — Build-artifact assertions (Vitest)
nodes.rationale: Cheapest possible check: src/test/pwa-build.test.ts asserts dist/sw.js and dist/manifest.webmanifest are emitted and the manifest shape is right. Already exists, already in CI, no change needed — it proves artifacts exist but nothing about runtime behavior.

nodes.label: Tier 1 — Playwright + headless Chromium (the workhorse)
nodes.rationale: Serve the production build, drive it headless, toggle context.setOffline(). Proves everything except the OS install dialog: SW registration/control after reload, manifest link + required fields (name, start_url, display standalone, 192+512 icons), offline app-shell render, offline IndexedDB persistence, and Slice A no-regression.

nodes.label: Tier 2 — Lighthouse installability audit
nodes.rationale: Playwright cannot cleanly assert 'is this installable per Chrome's bar'. Lighthouse's PWA category can: parse lh.json and fail the job if installable-manifest or service-worker score below 1.

nodes.label: Tier 3 — Android AVD + adb (true install + airplane mode)
nodes.rationale: Belt-and-suspenders real-device behavior without a phone: headless Pixel AVD reaches the host dev server at 10.0.2.2:4173, the install tap is done by hand because scriptable installs need extra tooling, and airplane mode is toggled via adb. Local/manual only, never CI. Windows desktop needs no emulator — Edge/Chrome install icon plus DevTools offline.
nodes.norm_label: tier 3 — android avd + adb (true install + airplane mode)

nodes.label: Offline cold-start persistence criterion
nodes.rationale: The definitive acceptance signal: add a task online, go offline, reload cold, and the task must still list. This proves the SW app shell AND IndexedDB survived together, which neither artifact checks nor installability audits can show.

nodes.label: Merge gate for #6 (Tier 0+1+2 required, Tier 3 nice-to-have)
nodes.rationale: Tiers 0-2 are CI-able and cover the substance, so they are required. Tier 3 is run locally once before declaring Slice B done rather than being a blocking gate.
nodes.norm_label: merge gate for #6 (tier 0+1+2 required, tier 3 nice-to-have)

nodes.label: LifeOS Telegram capture bot service
nodes.rationale: Standalone Node/TypeScript process with its own package.json, tsconfig.json and vitest.config.ts, deliberately decoupled from the Vite/React PWA build. It imports only the PWA's pure modules (src/vault/serialize.ts, the VaultTransport interface from src/vault/transport.ts, src/data/domains.ts) and never anything Vite/browser-specific, so the shared contract stays portable across runtimes.

nodes.label: Long-poll worker runtime shape (not a webhook)
nodes.rationale: ADR-0011 Decision 1: long-polling getUpdates keeps the local git clone warm across messages and avoids securing a public HTTPS endpoint for a single-owner bot. Consequence: it needs an always-on host and a writable disk, but zero inbound ports — all traffic is outbound HTTPS to api.telegram.org and the vault git remote.
nodes.norm_label: long-poll worker runtime shape (not a webhook)

nodes.label: Owner chat-id guard
nodes.rationale: OWNER_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID names the single chat the bot serves. Every other chat id is a complete no-op — no reply, no Claude call, no vault write — so an unauthorized sender cannot even burn API spend or leak the bot's existence via a response.

nodes.label: Separate bot/PWA vault PATs
nodes.rationale: BOT_VAULT_PAT is a fine-grained GitHub PAT (Contents read+write, vault repo only) deliberately distinct from the PWA's VITE_VAULT_PAT (ADR-0011 §2) so the two surfaces can be rotated or revoked independently. All secrets load once at boot via loadConfig, are validated loudly naming every missing var, and are never logged.

nodes.label: Voice-note capture pipeline
nodes.rationale: A voice note is fetched via telegramClient's two-step file download, transcribed by Groq-hosted Whisper (whisper-large-v3-turbo), then funnelled into the SAME classifyAndExtract → dispatch pipeline a typed message takes. The reply echoes the transcript back (heard: '<transcript>' → ...) for transparency.

nodes.label: Transcript confidence gate (mean no_speech_prob)
nodes.rationale: Confidence is computed from the transcript's mean no_speech_prob. A non-confident transcript short-circuits with a 'retype instead' prompt BEFORE any Claude call or vault write, so a mumbled or silent note can never cost API spend or write garbage into the vault.

nodes.label: Local-authoritative commit, best-effort push
nodes.rationale: Same discipline GitTransport.writeFile established in S15b: mkdir -p missing parents → git.add → a local git.commit that always succeeds offline against the full local clone → a best-effort git.push whose failure (offline / non-fast-forward) is swallowed. The unpushed commit IS the retry queue — no separate queue infrastructure is needed.

nodes.label: Wipe-and-reclone guard on readFiles
nodes.rationale: readFiles pulls fast-forward-only; on failure it first best-effort-pushes local commits and only wipes-and-reclones when nothing local is ahead of origin. This is the S15b 'must-fix transport hazard' — a plain wipe would silently destroy committed offline writes. The same path doubles as the first-boot shallow single-branch clone.

nodes.label: HITL-by-construction verification boundary (S16c vs S18)
nodes.rationale: S16c is HITL because CI has no git remote, no live Telegram token and no live Anthropic key — only local git logic is CI-verifiable (commit-lands, offline-commit-survives against an unreachable .invalid host, wipe-guard). S18 ships WITHOUT a HITL gate because downloadVoiceFile and transcribe are read-only network calls adding no vault-write surface; transcription quality against real audio is a non-blocking follow-up smoke test.

nodes.label: Inline (key:: value) field syntax
nodes.rationale: The universal vault encoding across every fixture except finance-networth: a markdown list item whose free-text label is followed by zero or more Dataview-style (key:: value) pairs. Parsers read fields by name, tolerate unknown extras (e.g. (mood:: focused)), and treat missing optional fields as absent rather than as an error. Keeping one syntax for habits, calendar, mail, finance, and career means a single field-extraction primitive serves all six parsers.

nodes.label: Malformed-line tolerance contract
nodes.rationale: Every fixture deliberately ends with junk — prose lines, wrong bullet markers (* instead of -), empty checkbox stubs, entries missing the required field, unknown enum values. The contract is that a parser must never throw on a hand-edited vault file and must silently skip anything not conforming, because the vault is edited by humans and by agents in Obsidian, not produced by a serializer alone.

nodes.label: INR shorthand amount parsing (₹1.2k / ₹2.05L / ₹17.2L)
nodes.rationale: All four finance fixtures pair plain integer amounts with human-typed rupee shorthand — ₹1.2k in bills, ₹2.05L in burn, ₹5.52L in portfolio, ₹17.2L in the networth table — so parseINR must normalise currency symbol, thousands (k) and lakh (L) suffixes to a number, and return null (not NaN, not 0) for blank or non-numeric values.

nodes.label: Pinned reference 'today' in fixtures
nodes.rationale: habits-log.md states in a comment that reference 'today' for the committed fixtures is 2026-07-15 (calendar-today.md is dated 2026-07-14). Streak/weekGrid/dueInDays are date-relative, so the golden files pin a date and the parsers take `today` as an explicit argument instead of reading the clock — otherwise the goldens would rot overnight.

nodes.label: Canonical seven-domain enum validation
nodes.rationale: Habit and course definitions carry (domain:: <one of the 7 canonical domains>); habits.md plants '(domain:: Nonsense)' so the parser is forced to decide what an out-of-enum domain means rather than trusting the file. The enum itself lives in src/data/domains.ts, shared with the bot.

nodes.label: Proposal status lifecycle (pending | approved | rejected)
nodes.rationale: Agent proposals are YAML-frontmatter documents (agent, date, status) with a fixed ## Change / ## Diff / ## Why body. Two byte-identical fixtures differing ONLY in the status line exist so the round-trip pair (parseProposal reading it, setProposalStatus rewriting it) can be tested as an exact transformation — approving a proposal must touch the status value and nothing else, including the trailing '# pending | approved | rejected' comment.

nodes.label: Fixture — habits.md (habit definitions)
nodes.rationale: Golden input for parseHabits. Shape: '# ' comment header lines, then one '- <name>' bullet per habit with optional (domain:: ...) and optional (min:: 45m) duration. Edge cases planted: a habit with an invalid domain ('Nonsense') and a bare habit with no fields at all, so both optional fields must be genuinely optional.

nodes.label: Fixture — habits-log.md (append-only hit log)
nodes.rationale: Golden input for parseHabitLog plus the derived streak/weekGrid calculations. Shape: '- [x] <habit name> (date:: YYYY-MM-DD) (source:: pwa|telegram|...)'. It encodes four distinct streak scenarios against the pinned 2026-07-15 today — hot streak n=3 unbroken, yesterday-only n=1 still alive, last-hit-two-days-ago n=1 broken, and a scattered week exercising weekGrid slot alignment — plus a tolerated-junk block: prose, an unchecked '- [ ]' line that must NOT count as a hit, a nameless hit, a hit with no date, and a '*' bullet.

nodes.label: Fixture — calendar-today.md (day's events)
nodes.rationale: Golden input for parseEventLine/parseCalendar (and downstream freeGaps). Shape: an '# YYYY-MM-DD' date heading then '- HH:MM-HH:MM <title> (type:: gym|call|deep|errand)' lines. The four events leave deliberate gaps between them so free-gap computation has something to find; the trailing 'this line is not a valid calendar event' forces the time-range regex to reject non-matching lines.

nodes.label: Fixture — mail-attention.md (email-triage attention queue)
nodes.rationale: Golden input for parseAttentionLine/parseAttention; written by the email-triage agent, not the owner. Shape: '- [ ]|[x] <summary> (label:: ...) (from:: ...) (waiting:: 26h|3d|0h) (draft:: <vault path>)'. Encodes the label taxonomy (client-money, bill, job, agent-failure, newsletter-digest, other), a done item, an optional draft-path pointer, mixed hour/day waiting units including 0h, an item with NO waiting field, an empty '- [ ]' stub, and a plain note line that is not a task.

nodes.label: Fixture — finance-bills.md (upcoming bills)
nodes.rationale: Golden input for parseBills (and dueInDays). Shape: '- [ ]|[x] <name> (amount:: ...) (due:: YYYY-MM-DD) (source:: gmail|manual)'. Edge cases: a paid bill, a shorthand ₹1.2k amount, a due date that is not a date at all, and a bill with the amount field entirely missing — so unpaid/paid, unparseable date, and null amount are all exercised.

nodes.label: Fixture — finance-burn.md (monthly income vs spend)
nodes.rationale: Golden input for parseBurn. Shape: '- income|spend (month:: YYYY-MM) (amount:: ...)'. Encodes months with both sides present (2026-07, 2026-06), a spend-only month (2026-05), a ₹2.05L shorthand income, a bogus kind that is neither income nor spend, and a month whose amount is not a number — so month grouping must tolerate half-populated and unparseable rows.

nodes.label: Fixture — finance-networth.md (append-only markdown table)
nodes.rationale: The only fixture that is a markdown TABLE rather than (key:: value) bullets: a | date | networth | header, a separator row, then newest-first data rows. parseNetworthHistory must skip the header and separator, and reject a non-date row and a row with an empty networth cell. Feeds networthDelta, so ordering of the surviving points matters.

nodes.label: Fixture — finance-portfolio.md (allocation slices)
nodes.rationale: Golden input for parsePortfolio. Shape: '- <slice name> (value:: ...) (pct:: <int>)'. Edge cases: a ₹5.52L shorthand value, a slice with an EMPTY value field but a present pct, a junk line with no fields, and percentages that deliberately sum to 105 rather than 100 — the parser must not silently renormalise or assume the file is internally consistent.

nodes.label: Fixture — career-pipeline.md (job pipeline)
nodes.rationale: Golden input for parsePipeline/groupByStage; co-written by the owner and the job-scout agent. Shape: '- <company> — <role> (stage:: found|applied|interview|closed) (age:: 6d) (match:: 82%) (hot:: true) (next:: ...) (source:: job-scout) (outcome:: rejected)'. Every canonical stage appears at least once, plus an out-of-enum '(stage:: weird)', a prose line that must be skipped, and a headless entry with fields but no company/role text.

nodes.label: Fixture — career-courses.md (course progress)
nodes.rationale: Golden input for parseCourses. Shape: '- <course name> (progress:: <0-100>) (next:: <action ~45min>) (domain:: ...)'. Boundary cases are the point: a completed 100, an over-range 140, a negative -10, a course with no progress field at all, and a prose line — so the parser must decide whether to clamp, drop, or pass through out-of-range progress.

nodes.label: Fixture — proposal-pending.md (agent proposal, pending)
nodes.rationale: Golden input for parseProposal. YAML frontmatter (agent: email-triage, date, status: pending with a trailing enum comment) plus a fixed body of ## Change (prose), ## Diff (a fenced -/+ block), and ## Why (the justification). The status line carries an inline '# pending | approved | rejected' comment that the parser must strip when reading the value.

nodes.label: Fixture — proposal-approved.md (same proposal, approved)
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical to proposal-pending.md except 'status: pending' → 'status: approved'. It is the expected OUTPUT golden for setProposalStatus as much as an input for parseProposal — the pair pins that a status transition rewrites exactly one token and preserves frontmatter ordering, the inline enum comment, and the whole body verbatim.

nodes.label: Fixture — supervisor-report.md (weekly fleet report)
nodes.rationale: Golden input for parseReport. Unlike the (key:: value) fixtures this is section-structured prose: a path-style H1, then ## Fleet week (per-agent run/failure/latency/accuracy lines), ## Concerns, ## Proposals (an Obsidian [[wikilink]] to a proposal note, the join back to the proposal fixtures), and ## Notes. The parser must key off the H2 headings and follow the wikilink rather than parse the free text.

nodes.label: NOW view (command-center surface)
nodes.rationale: The home screen's job is to answer 'what do I do now?'. v1 deliberately shipped the simplest honest ranking first (pure priority, domain-blind) so the surface existed and was trusted BEFORE the balance brain made it smart. Top 3-5 live cards, remainder folded under 'Up next'/'Later' as collapsed counts.

nodes.label: Tab bar navigation shape (Now/Domains/Pulse/+)
nodes.rationale: The app's navigation frame every later screen plugs into: four thumb-reachable, safe-area-aware bottom tabs. Chose simple local view state over adding a router (no deep-linking need, no heavy dep), and kept each tab's view a standalone component so later slices edit one screen without touching navigation.

nodes.label: Tap-the-dot complete + 3s Undo toast
nodes.rationale: Completion is the most frequent action, so the gesture is a precise status-dot tap (no accidental completes, identical desktop/mobile): dot fills to a check, ring pulse, card fades and folds. Undo is implemented by re-issuing toggleDone(id) within the 3s window rather than inventing a separate 'undo' seam method — keeps the seam surface minimal. Respects prefers-reduced-motion; keeps navigator.vibrate haptic.

nodes.label: Domain warmth (derived, never logged)
nodes.rationale: The core v1 feedback loop: warmth is DERIVED from the most recent completed_at in a domain, never logged by the user. Completing heats a domain, silence cools it, so neglect is felt before it becomes a problem. Surfaced as glow intensity + a one-word state (hot/warm/ok/stale/cold) on the Domains map — deliberately no raw numbers. Requires Task.completed_at (set on complete, cleared on un-complete) and feeds the balance brain.

nodes.label: PWA shell (installable + offline)
nodes.rationale: vite-plugin-pwa (Workbox) precaching the app shell, manifest with standalone display and 192/512 + maskable icons. Split into its own slice AFTER the task loop because it shares vite.config.ts with the task-loop slice — serialized purely to avoid a same-file conflict, not because of a logical dependency. Riskiest v1 assumption: one web codebase can be installable, offline and polished on both Windows and Android.

nodes.label: Apple-feel polish as acceptance, not decoration
nodes.rationale: SF system font stack, generous whitespace, spring on complete (transform/opacity only), navigator.vibrate haptic on mobile, calm 'All clear' empty state. Explicitly written as the definition of done for every capability: if the core loop doesn't feel instant and trustworthy, nothing built on top will. Adding a task must beat opening a notes app.
nodes.norm_label: apple-feel polish as acceptance, not decoration

nodes.label: Tracer-bullet slice (vertical, single-issue)
nodes.rationale: Each slice is a thin vertical (UI + logic + seam + tests) sized to one agent. Slices are split only when it buys real parallelism: S15/S17 stayed atomic because their write-sets fully overlapped (types/seam/hook/App) or their parts were mutually load-bearing, so splitting would only force serialization and duplicate the same shared-file hunks across two tickets.

nodes.label: AFK deploy table (issue / task / context / model / parallel group)
nodes.rationale: The pipeline's hand-off artifact: one row per dispatchable issue carrying a self-contained context cell (literal file list, ADR/PRD refs, blocked-by, do-NOT-touch fence, exact test files) plus a model tier and a batch label. Deliberately stops at the table — implementer agents are not auto-dispatched — so a human can sequence batches.
nodes.norm_label: afk deploy table (issue / task / context / model / parallel group)

nodes.label: Dual-green merge gate (CI + ponytail-review ultra)
nodes.rationale: No PR merges on local tests alone — local tests are necessary, not sufficient. A PR needs CI green AND a ponytail-review (ultra) green-light before the orchestrator merges to master.

nodes.label: CI Build Supervisor (paired agent)
nodes.rationale: Every implementer dispatch is paired with a supervisor agent scoped to that PR whose job is triaging flake-vs-real CI failures (e.g. the known wrapper-validation network flake), rerunning known flakes, and alerting on green — so the implementer isn't the judge of its own CI.

nodes.label: HITL flag (not CI-verifiable)
nodes.rationale: HITL in v1 came to mean 'cannot be exercised in CI', not 'needs design judgment'. The recurring cases: real-device install/airplane-mode checks, the live git write path needing a write-scoped PAT against the real vault repo, and the live Telegram + Anthropic loop. Design unknowns were instead pre-resolved into ADRs, with bounded implementation defaults (TTLs, thresholds, model pins) recorded as explicitly non-blocking assumptions carrying a 'revisit if insufficient in practice' fallback.

nodes.label: Write-set + do-NOT-touch fence
nodes.rationale: Each ticket declares a literal write-set and an explicit list of files it must not touch (frozen seam, frozen Dexie schema, another slice's territory). This is what makes concurrent agents safe: collision is prevented by contract at ticket-authoring time rather than detected at merge time.

nodes.label: Cross-pipeline hotspot: serialize, don't same-batch
nodes.rationale: services/bot/router.ts became a shared hotspot: S17 (confirm gate), S18 (voice branch) and S19 (photo branch) each add additive, non-conflicting-in-intent branches to the same handleIncomingMessage function — but as literal same-file hunks from sibling branches they conflict. Rule: never dispatch two hotspot slices in the same parallelism phase; serialize and rebase the second. The considered alternative was extracting a shared prerequisite (an `earlyIntercepts` array router.ts iterates that each slice registers into) — flagged for the orchestrator, deliberately not resolved unilaterally by a single pipeline run.

nodes.label: Sonnet-readiness check
nodes.rationale: A ticket is dispatchable to a cheaper model only if it is fully pre-resolved: every design call already made in an ADR, literal file paths/function signatures/thresholds given, testable acceptance criteria naming the exact test files, and an explicit do-NOT-touch fence. Anything left to invent is a business/product unknown and must not be handed to an agent.

nodes.label: Telegram capture bot
nodes.rationale: A bot-in-the-pocket so a thought is captured the instant it occurs, including hands-busy. Runtime is a long-poll Node/TS worker over Telegram getUpdates, NOT a serverless webhook — this keeps the local git clone warm across messages, needs no public HTTPS endpoint for a single-owner bot, and avoids serverless execution-time ceilings for git+Claude round trips. Auth is its own write-scoped fine-grained PAT (BOT_VAULT_PAT), separate from the PWA's VITE_VAULT_PAT; all secrets via env, never committed. An owner guard makes any non-owner message a complete no-op.

nodes.label: Intent router seam (self-registering intents)
nodes.rationale: One file per intent under services/bot/intents/, each self-registering into a shared Map, so the only per-slice shared touchpoint is a single append-only import line in intents/index.ts. Carved early and deliberately so the later modality slices (S17/S18/S19) would not collide on a shared registry. Dispatch-by-name also means a new front door (voice, photo) reaches whatever intents happen to be registered, for free.

nodes.label: Durable `id::` identity in vault markdown
nodes.rationale: Landed exactly when the bot became the second live mutator of the vault — ADR-0010's own stated upgrade trigger — because in-memory source-map identity is only safe with a single writer. parseTaskLine reads an optional id::; serializeTaskLine always emits it; legacy lines get a lazy on-next-write backfill. Chosen as a vault-markdown-format addition only: no Task shape change, no Dexie schema bump, at a known cost in markdown legibility.

nodes.label: Confirm-destructive gate (update/delete)
nodes.rationale: Create fires immediately, but update and delete go through a fuzzy task matcher plus a per-chat pending-confirmation gate that commits only on an explicit 'y'. The gate is checked in router.ts before the NLU call, so a destructive action can never be triggered by a single ambiguous message. Bounded defaults recorded as non-blocking assumptions: 2-minute confirm TTL, match thresholds 0.6/0.5, candidate cap of 5.

nodes.label: Voice notes: confidence-gated transcription ingest
nodes.rationale: Voice is purely a new front door on the message-ingest layer — download, transcribe, then feed the transcript into the UNMODIFIED classifyAndExtract/dispatchIntent pipeline, so no intent logic forks. Groq's hosted Whisper (whisper-large-v3-turbo) called via native fetch, no new SDK, behind a Transcriber interface so swapping providers touches one file. No transcoding needed: Telegram voice notes are already OGG/Opus, which Groq accepts natively. Because a mis-heard word could silently trigger a destructive action once update/delete land, the transcript reaches the NLU only when confident (non-empty text AND mean no_speech_prob <= 0.5); otherwise a fixed retype reply with no Claude call and no vault write. Transcribe never throws — errors map to not-confident. Every successful action echoes 'heard: ...' so a mis-hear is caught before it is trusted. Depends on S16 only, deliberately decoupled from S17.

nodes.label: Photo ingest: vision extract + batch confirm
nodes.rationale: A photo yields structured multi-task output via Claude vision, reusing nlu.ts's domain/priority normalization, then a per-chat pending batch (10-minute TTL, one pending batch per chat) that the owner confirms before each task is created through the existing handleCreate. Split into ingest (#71) and confirm+router-wiring (#72) with disjoint write-sets — a real import dependency, not hotspot avoidance. Bounded defaults: 20-task cap, 10-minute TTL, claude-sonnet-5 vision pin.
nodes.norm_label: photo ingest: vision extract + batch confirm
